memory_candidates.content: A cross-file consistency sweep's own gate grep is only as complete as the file-type globs it names. This task's Phase 6 gate ran `--include="*.py" --include="*.md"` over the whole subtree and still missed examples.py's module docstring, because the docstring's exact phrasing ('Maximum length of a witness-family lasso's repeating back segment') differed just enough in word order from the grep's alternation to not obviously stand out during manual review of the hit list, even though the grep pattern itself did technically match it as a .py hit — the miss was in triage, not tooling. Lesson: when a gate grep's hit list is long (this sweep produced ~100 lines of raise/raising/exception-handling noise), do not eyeball it — pipe through a second, narrower grep for the exact false-claim phrase (e.g. `grep -i 'maximum length of a'`) to separate signal from the noise before declaring the sweep complete.
